Cisco Networking Academy · Completed Sept 12, 2026 · 70 hours

Achievements

Swipe or scroll sideways → · Tap a picture to enlarge

Introduction to Ethical Hacking and Penetration Testing

What I learned

I learned what ethical hacking is, why organizations hire penetration testers, and the legal and ethical rules that keep testing authorized.

Planning and Scoping a Pentest Assessment

What I learned

I learned that a pentest starts by agreeing on goals, scope, and rules of engagement so the work stays legal and focused.

Information Gathering and Vulnerability Scanning

What I learned

I learned how testers collect information about a target and use scanning tools to find weaknesses worth investigating.

Social Engineering Attacks

What I learned

I learned how attackers manipulate people instead of technology, for example through phishing, and why awareness is a key defense.

Exploiting Wired and Wireless Networks

What I learned

I learned about common weaknesses in wired and Wi-Fi networks and how attackers take advantage of them.

Exploiting Application-Based Vulnerabilities

What I learned

I learned how flaws in web and software applications can be abused, and why secure coding and testing help prevent them.

Cloud, Mobile, and IoT Security

What I learned

I learned the special security risks of cloud services, mobile devices, and IoT gadgets, which often receive less protection.

Performing Post-Exploitation Techniques

What I learned

I learned what testers do after gaining access, such as checking how far an attacker could go, and how to clean up afterward.

Reporting and Communication

What I learned

I learned that a pentest is only useful when the findings are clearly reported, with the risks explained and fixes recommended.

Tools and Code Analysis

What I learned

I learned about the common tools, scripts, and code analysis that testers use to find and verify security issues.
